therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: B-cell depletion via anti-CD20 antibody binding
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with active rheumatoid arthritis on stable methotrexate background therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: ACR20 response rate at Week 24 and Week 48

results.effect_size: ACR20 at Week 24: 56.9% (200 mg) and 54.5% (500 mg) vs 35.7% placebo; weighted difference ~18.5–21.4 percentage points. ACR20 at Week 48: 58.3% (200 mg) and 62.1% (500 mg) vs 27.6% placebo; weighted difference ~30.8–34.5 percentage points
results.target_engagement_evidence: Reductions in ESR and CRP consistent with B-cell/immune depletion; DAS28 improvements greater in ocrelizumab arms
biomarker_changes: CRP decreased from baseline at Week 24: -30.41 mg/dL (200 mg), -23.07 mg/dL (500 mg) vs +11.64 mg/dL (placebo)
ESR decreased from baseline at Week 24: -20.10% (200 mg), -29.98% (500 mg) vs -2.51% (placebo)
DAS28 change at Week 48: -2.42 (200 mg), -2.68 (500 mg) vs -1.38 (placebo)
mTSS change at Week 48: +0.26 (200 mg), -0.03 (500 mg) vs +1.74 (placebo)
subgroup_findings: DAS28 remission at Week 48: 16.0% (200 mg), 17.5% (500 mg) vs 5.3% (placebo)
ACR70 at Week 48: 20.7% (200 mg), 22.4% (500 mg) vs 6.6% (placebo)
HAQ-DI improvement ≥0.25 at Week 48: 58.9% (200 mg), 65.9% (500 mg) vs 34.8% (placebo)
No radiographic progression at Week 48: 58.7% (200 mg), 60.8% (500 mg) vs 37.7% (placebo)
safety_signals: Serious infections and malignancies observed across arms
Trial terminated due to unfavorable overall benefit-to-risk profile in RA
Serious cardiovascular events (aortic aneurysm, aortic dissection) in 200 mg arm
B-cell lymphoma observed across all arms
Breast cancer in both ocrelizumab arms

context.duration: 48 weeks treatment with up to 8.5 years follow-up for safety
context.investigator_commentary: Based on analysis of results and consideration of available treatments, the overall benefit to risk profile of ocrelizumab was not favorable in RA.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Methotrexate background therapy may enhance ocrelizumab's B-cell depletion efficacy by suppressing residual T-cell and inflammatory activity, creating a more permissive environment for B-cell-targeted immunosuppression
modulation_entries.citation: Methotrexate tablet was administered orally at a dose 7.5-25 mg [as background therapy in all active arms alongside ocrelizumab]
